evidence: Read the original Ben-Shushan PDF page 10 Removal of measurement noise, Eqs.18-19. Independent endpoint errors add two copies of their position variance to positive-lag MSD; at exactly zero the two endpoint errors are the same sample and cancel.

A07.author: /root/all_draw_eye_place
A07.strongest_objection: An arbitrary smooth curve might be passed off as a Gaussian-process simulation, or spatial position could be mistaken for a neural trajectory.
A07.objection_resolution: The explicit finite-grid Cholesky covariance, fixed seed and normalization establish the stated simulated input. The upper label says one fixed simulated map, the x-axis says position/sigma, and connected text explicitly separates spatial maps from time dynamics. No claim of empirical recovery or a full GP test is made.

claims.claim: normalized input z(x); ticks -2,0,2
claims.evidence: Chapter defines z=h/sigma_h, dimensionless, with unit ensemble variance. A single finite map need not have exact zero spatial mean or unit spatial sample variance.

claims.claim: one fixed simulated map
claims.evidence: One Gaussian vector is drawn and held fixed, not a temporal simulation or measured neuron.

claims.claim: q=0.8 and dashed threshold
claims.evidence: The drawn height is dimensionless .8 and matches the chosen rectification threshold.

claims.claim: position / sigma; ticks 0,4,8,12,16,20,24
claims.evidence: The track spans 24 correlation-length units. Its horizontal axis is spatial distance normalized by the taught sigma.

claims.claim: firing rate F(x) (Hz); visible ticks 0,1,2,3,4
claims.evidence: Rate is a=6 Hz times a dimensionless positive excess. It is nonnegative and peaks near 3.09 Hz.
At each sampled point F is six times max(z-.8,0), exactly the chosen model.

claims.claim: Introduction: Gaussian covariance exp[-(delta x/sigma)^2/2], q=.8,a=6, position units sigma
claims.evidence: Finite-grid normalized covariance and gains match the model and generator; sigma is defined before this insertion.

claims.claim: Caption: fixed Gaussian input becomes nonnegative through rectification; subthreshold zero; relative heights; shaded connected intervals are fields
claims.evidence: The function and support match upper/lower panels. Differences between suprathreshold values are scaled by a; the fields are excursion components, not individual spikes.

claims.claim: Caption: simulated chosen parameters, not recorded cell; Mainali Fig.1A and Eqs.2-3
claims.evidence: Direct source inspection confirms the same mathematical operation. Chosen values are not presented as paper estimates.

claims.claim: Alt: fixed spatial function, threshold .8, sixfold positive excess, aligned connected support
claims.evidence: All listed relationships are visible in both full and preview pixels.

claims.claim: Interpretation: changed value distribution; separated fields; same fixed spatial map, neither trajectory
claims.evidence: Rectification introduces mass at zero and the four disconnected active intervals; the original GP remains fixed.

evidence: Read original Mainali PDF page 13, Model details Eqs.2-3: stationary Gaussian h is rectified after subtracting q times its SD. Read the current PLACE-GP normalization z=h/sigma_h, rate F=a[z-q]+, excursion-set definition and sigma definition. Normalized unit variance makes the displayed construction equivalent.

The generator uses a fixed 601-point multivariate Gaussian draw with squared-exponential covariance on spacing .04 sigma, seed16 and diagonal jitter 1e-10. The 4 positive components match the upper threshold crossings and lower support. Jitter is a numerical regularization, not a claim that a continuum path acquires independent roughness.
The latest insertion anchor follows the sigma definition, so x/sigma, q and a have already been introduced. Both axes represent the same fixed map over physical position, not time.
Also read actual Mainali supplement PDF page9, printed8, MethodsS1: finite-position values jointly Gaussian and x indexes animal location; threshold nonlinearity maps excursions to fields.

A08.author: /root/all_draw_eye_place
A08.strongest_objection: Divergent 3D density could be misread as many exactly zero-volume fields, or the universal transformed law as a finite-threshold empirical collapse.
A08.objection_resolution: The chapter immediately after the size table explains no zero-size point mass, and the figure caption explicitly says the high-threshold limiting law, not finite-threshold simulations or measured histograms. The plot labels a density and marks the unbounded limit, while the survival axes show the nonlinear U transformation.

claims.claim: dimensionless size w=beta^(d/2)s; ticks0,1,2,3,4,5
claims.evidence: beta has distance^-2 and s distance^d, so w is dimensionless. This is a size rescaling, not the U power transformation.

claims.claim: density of w; ticks0,1,2
claims.evidence: The Jacobian gives (2/d)w^(2/d-1)exp(-w^(2/d)); values are densities, not bin probabilities.

claims.claim: d=1 solid navy; d=2 dashed teal; d=3 dotted orange
claims.evidence: Curves use the correct dimensional exponents and are consistently identified in both legends.

claims.claim: unbounded as w approaches0; arrow
claims.evidence: d3 exponent of w is -1/3. Arrow targets the divergent portion and does not imply an assigned finite value at zero.
From w=beta^(d/2)s, its power2/d is exactly beta s^(2/d). The symbol u is a threshold value for random U.

claims.claim: survival probability Pr(U>u); ticks0.0,0.5,1.0
claims.evidence: The second axis is a probability, and all displayed exponential values lie in[0,1].

claims.claim: Pr(U>u)=exp(-u)
claims.evidence: Integrating the transformed density gives exp(-u), confirmed by independent algebra and numerical identities.

claims.claim: Introduction: scale removal versus shared transformed exponential law
claims.evidence: The size rescaling and nonlinear transformation are explicitly distinguished and match the displayed axes.

claims.claim: Caption: length Rayleigh; area exponential; volume integrable divergence
claims.evidence: Shapes are 2/d=2,1,2/3. Integral near zero in d3 vanishes with cutoff^(2/3), so divergence is integrable.

claims.claim: Caption: survival coincidence under U; exact limiting calculation, not finite-threshold data; main Eq.1
claims.evidence: Direct formula, code and original source agree with the local high-threshold qualification. Caption notation is plain text powers; Stage2 can render these as math without changing content.

claims.claim: Alt: different origin behaviors, arrow, three coincident survival curves
claims.evidence: Actual two panels match all listed origin behaviors and line identities.

claims.claim: Interpretation: units removed while shapes differ; nonlinear U removes shape difference; common exponential assumption
claims.evidence: The same exponential U was the starting distribution in the guide derivation, so the collapse is an analytic identity, not a further empirical validation.

evidence: Read original Mainali PDF page3 Eq.1 and the guide PLACE-SIZE-LAW change of variables. For s>0, p_d(s)=(2 beta/d)s^(2/d-1)exp(-beta s^(2/d)). For w=beta^(d/2)s, density is (2/d)w^(2/d-1)exp(-w^(2/d)). This removes scale but preserves the d-dependent shape.

Independently integrated the displayed dimensionless densities and their means without importing the drawing code. All masses are one to numerical precision and means match Gamma(1+d/2). Pr(w>v)=exp(-v^(2/d)); U=w^(2/d) has Pr(U>u)=exp(-u).

d1 density is zero at the origin and peaks at 1/sqrt(2); d2 starts at one; d3 behaves as (2/3)w^(-1/3) near zero. This singularity is integrable and has no point mass. The arrow explicitly marks the clipped divergent end. Coincident survival traces use distinct dashes and widths without shifting data.

Also read actual Mainali supplement PDF page13, printed12, high-threshold distribution and moment text immediately before S18. The displayed law and transformed exponential agree; this figure does not use the printed S18 scale formula that the guide qualifies.
